title: Day one
arc: Your first week as Meridian's staff data architect. Asha, the CTO, hired you to turn a pile of scripts into a data platform the company can trust, and she wants to know where you stand before she hands you anything that matters. Dev shows you round on-call, Mei asks what all this will cost, and Grace, an architect who has done this twice before, offers to be your sounding board. The week ends with a diagnostic that tells you, and Asha, where to start.
previously: Before your first day ends: what would Meridian need from data in a year, in one sentence?
Yesterday you set up the machine. Which step would you write down first for the next hire?
Recall: what are the two rules about using AI in this program?
Yesterday's diagnostic counted trips per city. What data structure did you reach for, and why?
cliff: Asha wants the platform in one picture. What are its five layers?
Your setup script failed on step three. What will you check first tomorrow?
The diagnostic is tomorrow. Which kind of task will slow you down most?
Tomas from product says the fare script takes forty minutes. Where would you look first?

scenes.monday: Asha drops a sticky note on your new desk: "In a year, what does Meridian need from data?" She wants an answer you can defend, not a slide. Start with how the program works and the platform you will build.
scenes.midweek: Your laptop refuses the setup script, and Dev, who is supposed to be on leave, talks you through it from a café. You get a working environment and a promise to write down every step for the next hire.
scenes.friday: Friday is your own diagnostic: a handful of Python tasks that show where you are strong and where to start. Asha says she cares less about the score than about how you work.
